author: ribeye
dek: When Microsoft 365 went down worldwide, one Dublin household lost its email, its calendar, and its last excuse for missing the PTA meeting.
disclaimer: Parody: the Brennan family of Dublin is fictional. The Microsoft 365 outage is real, as reported by the Associated Press in November 2026.
headline: Dublin Family Discovers Just How Much of Life Runs Through Outlook

ohio_quotes.quote: I refreshed Outlook so many times I think I wore out the F5 key. Then I called the help desk, and the help desk was also refreshing Outlook.
ohio_quotes.speaker: Tom Brennan, Dublin

ohio_quotes.quote: We had to do it the old way. I called people. On the phone. With my voice. One of the moms thought something was wrong.
ohio_quotes.speaker: Karen Brennan, Dublin

ohio_story: DUBLIN, Ohio — Tom Brennan knew something was wrong when his inbox stopped loading at 12:47 p.m. on Thursday and, for the first time in eleven years, nobody in his office could blame him for not answering an email. Brennan, who works in IT for a company near Bridge Park, spent the afternoon refreshing Outlook, restarting his laptop twice, and finally — in a moment he describes as "deeply humbling" — calling the help desk to ask if the help desk was also down. It was.

His wife, Karen, had her own crisis: the Dublin Coffman PTA sign-up sheet lived in a shared mailbox, the third-grade field trip permission slips were trapped in a Teams channel, and the family's entire weekend — a birthday party in Powell, a soccer game at the Dublin Community Recreation Center, and a cousin's visit from Grove City — existed only as calendar invites nobody could open. "We had to do it the old way," Karen said. "I called people. On the phone. With my voice. One of the moms thought something was wrong." Their son, 14-year-old Eli, was briefly the happiest person in the house, having discovered that his homework assignment had been emailed to him and was now, technically, undeliverable.

By Friday morning, with email queues finally clearing, the Brennans had a new family rule, written on the fridge in dry-erase marker next to the Buckeyes schedule: important plans go on paper, too. Tom has already printed the weekend calendar and taped it to the pantry door. "Microsoft can have my inbox," he said, "but it cannot have my Saturday. I checked. Twice. On paper."
real_summary: A global Microsoft outage disrupted Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook, Teams, and the AI assistant Copilot, after problems first emerged midday Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026, in the United States. As the outage entered its second day on Friday, Microsoft said it saw "encouraging recovery progress," but warned that "intermittent access issues or delayed email delivery" might persist for some users.

The reach of the outage was swift: online tracker Downdetector said it received outage reports from 74 countries and territories within an hour. The total number of people affected was not clear, but Microsoft said in January it had more than 450 million paid commercial subscriptions to its 365 services. Microsoft said a technical issue arose during an upgrade that followed "a recent network change," and that a number of its servers became "unexpectedly unavailable" during automated checks. The company said there was no indication the disruption was caused by malicious activity, specifically noting Friday that it was not related to a cyberattack or artificial intelligence agents.

The disruption piled up far beyond office inboxes. In Britain, the outage brought a halt to a trial in Manchester, police said they were unable to receive crime reports online, and the National Health Service was affected, with the National Pharmacy Association warning of delays in getting medication. Governments in Singapore, Japan, Greece, and Norway said the outage affected some of their operations, and OpenAI and Anthropic reported problems connecting with Microsoft 365 tools.
source_note: AP reporting, Nov. 14, 2026: global Microsoft 365 outage that began Nov. 12; Outlook, Teams, and Copilot disrupted; recovery progress and worldwide impact.
